guides.save-the-date-maker.title: Save-the-Date Cards: Timing and Wording
guides.save-the-date-maker.desc: When to send save-the-dates, what must be on them, and how to word a card before the guest list and venue details are fully final.
guides.save-the-date-maker.lead: A save-the-date has one job: get the date into people's calendars before they book something else. Details can follow later.
guides.save-the-date-maker.f1v: Six to eight months ahead; twelve for destination weddings
guides.save-the-date-maker.f2v: Names, date, city or region, and a website URL
guides.save-the-date-maker.f3v: Venue once confirmed; plus-one and child notes wait
guides.save-the-date-maker.f4v: A card, magnet or digital note — all work equally well
guides.save-the-date-maker.s1: Send only the information that will not change. Names, the date, the city or region, and a wedding website are enough; the exact venue, timings and dress code belong on the invitation. If a guest might need a visa, a group room block or a flight, send to them first and add travel notes to the website as soon as they exist.
guides.save-the-date-maker.s2: In the US save-the-dates are standard and often sent eight to twelve months ahead for destination weddings. UK couples frequently skip them or send a short digital note, relying on formal invitations six to eight weeks out. Guests in other countries may need considerably more lead time for long-haul travel and leave requests, so prioritise the list by travel distance rather than sending everything at once.
guides.save-the-date-maker.s3: Do not send a save-the-date to someone you might later cut from the guest list — it is effectively an invitation. Do not put a date in numeric form for an international list, and do not list a venue you have not signed with. Keep a record of exactly who received one, because that list should be a subset of the final invitation list.
guides.save-the-date-maker.a1: Six to eight months before the wedding, and up to twelve months for a destination wedding or a holiday weekend.
guides.save-the-date-maker.q2: What information belongs on the card?
guides.save-the-date-maker.a2: Your names, the date, the city or region, and a wedding website. Add 'formal invitation to follow' to set expectations.
guides.save-the-date-maker.a3: No. A digital note is equally valid and easier to update. Choose based on your guests, not on tradition.
